cards.title: Adopt a business for shutdown weekends
cards.summary: Shop Small Greenpoint's ask for closure weekends: commit to spending locally, post about your visits, and encourage friends to "adopt" a favorite shop. Can't make it? Order pickup/delivery or buy a gift card — immediate cash flow is what carries small shops through.

cards.title: Weigh in on how the G closures are run
cards.summary: What Shop Small Greenpoint is asking the MTA for: non-consecutive weekend closures, overnight-only work where possible, better shuttle frequency, clearer signage, and recognition of the retail-corridor impact. You can file a complaint or write to the electeds who represent Greenpoint (Restler, Gallagher, González).
cards.whyItMatters: Closures are recurring (more weekends reported for Aug–Dec) — how they're scheduled is still an open question.

cards.title: Monitor Point approved: 1,324 waterfront apartments
cards.kicker: Council signs off on Quay St towers
cards.summary: The City Council approved Monitor Point on June 25: roughly 1,324 apartments at 40–56 Quay St, 662 of them (50%) permanently affordable, plus over an acre of new waterfront open space, a new home for the Greenpoint Monitor Museum, $300K a year for Bushwick Inlet Park maintenance, and two MTA facilities relocated out of the area. Save the Inlet's petition against building on land promised as parkland in the 2005 rezoning drew more than 5,000 signatures.
cards.whyItMatters: The biggest land-use decision on the waterfront in a generation — years of construction first, thousands of new neighbors after.

timeline.title: The parkland fight
timeline.summary: Gotham Organization proposes three towers on the Monitor Point peninsula — land set aside for parks in the 2005 rezoning. Save the Inlet's opposition petition passes 5,000 signatures.

timeline.title: Council approval
timeline.summary: Final deal: ~1,324 units with 50% permanently affordable (up from the proposed 25%), waterfront open space, a Monitor Museum home, and Bushwick Inlet Park maintenance funding.

sourceLinks.title: City Council press release — Monitor Point approval

cards.title: McGuinness redesign construction is underway
cards.kicker: Bike lanes reach the Pulaski by fall
cards.summary: Crews are extending the parking-protected bike lanes from Meeker Ave to the Pulaski Bridge. The finished boulevard gets one travel lane, one protected bike lane, and one parking/loading lane in each direction, with shorter crossings and traffic calming. The city expects completion by early fall.
cards.whyItMatters: Greenpoint's most divisive street decision is becoming physical — how the corridor works for drivers, deliveries, and cyclists changes this season.

cards.title: EPA keeps testing the Meeker Avenue Plume

cards.title: Clay Space ceramics membership

cards.whyItMatters: The application gate and the one-year prerequisite are the part nobody tells you until you ask.

The Clay Space Annex is a 700 sq. ft. ground floor, private entrance studio space located just across the street from our center. $365 - $525 + tax monthly. $485 - $650 + tax monthly. membership will only be considered for those with more than one year of consistent lessons and are able to commit to a 3-month minimum membership term.
